events.title: BCP September Survey: Analysts Lift 2026 Growth to 4.5%, Cut Inflation to 3.0% and See the Guaraní at G. 6,100 by December (2026-09-17)
events.summary: The BCP's September Survey of Economic Variables Expectations (EVE) shows analysts raising their 2026 GDP growth forecast to 4.5%, up from 4.3% in August and above the IMF's 4.4%, keeping 2027 at 4.0%. The end-2026 inflation forecast was cut to 3.0% from 3.3%, with a 2.8% mean, well inside the central bank's 3.5% ±2pp target; agents expect 0.2% monthly inflation for both September and October. The projected nominal exchange rate was revised down to G. 6,015/USD for September and G. 6,100/USD for December (from G. 6,150), with G. 6,300 seen for end-2027. The policy rate is expected to stay at 5.50% through 2026 before easing to 5.25% in 2027, confirming a neutral stance that keeps carry-trade inflows supporting the guaraní.

events.title: Soy Complex Posts Record USD 3,877 Million in Eight Months, Equal to 40% of Paraguay's Total Export Earnings (2026-09-16)
events.summary: Capeco's foreign-trade report, released on 16 September, confirms the soy complex generated USD 3,877 million in the first eight months of 2026, 40% of all Paraguayan export revenue. Soybean grain shipments reached 7,413,675 tonnes, up from 5,406,291 tonnes a year earlier, worth USD 2,886 million, roughly USD 907 million more than in 2025. Soybean oil exports rose 6% to 449,142 tonnes and pellets 12% to 1,617,365 tonnes, both records. Argentina took 86% of grain shipments, Brazil 10%, with the remainder split among Russia, Saudi Arabia, Vietnam, the United States, Uruguay, Chile and South Korea; exports to Russia resumed. Fifty-three companies participated in the 2025/26 harvest. The concentration in Argentina remains a structural vulnerability for the sector and amplifies exposure to the guaraní's appreciation.

events.title: MEF Announces Fourth Treasury Bond Auction of 2026 for September 23, Reopening 2030 and 2035 Series (2026-09-18)
events.summary: The Ministry of Economy and Finance scheduled its fourth domestic Treasury bond placement of 2026 for Wednesday 23 September, reopening two series maturing in 2030 and 2035 with semi-annual coupons. The operation runs through the Asunción Stock Exchange (BVA), only the second time this channel has been used this year after placements had been conducted exclusively via the central bank. Proceeds help finance the 2026 budget and deepen the local capital market. Previous 2026 auctions raised G. 698,000 million in April and G. 974,350 million in June via the BCP, plus G. 360,548 million in July via the BVA, roughly G. 2 trillion (about USD 339 million) in total. The 2027 budget submitted to Congress foresees bond issuance of USD 2,708 million, 70% more than 2026, with 99% planned for international markets.

events.title: BCP Breaks Silence on Senate Information Requests and Reaffirms the Soundness of the Financial System (2026-09-18)
events.summary: After weeks of silence, central bank governor Carlos Carvallo and the Association of Banks (Asoban), represented by Liz Cramer, met President Santiago Peña and committed to answering the Senate's information requests on the operations of four private banks linked to the Ueno Bank case. Carvallo ratified the solvency of the financial system and the institution's willingness to provide the required documentation, while Asoban confirmed its members would cooperate. Peña said 'doubts must be cleared up'. The Senate's requests, driven by the ruling Honor Colorado caucus with opposition support, cover 31 questions on Ueno's related-party exposure, public-sector deposits, a USD 35 million portfolio sale and a July 2026 supervisory memorandum, as well as the GNB-BBVA, Sudameris-Regional, Continental-Río and Atlas-Familiar integrations. The BCP has 15 working days to respond under Article 192 of the Constitution.

events.title: Peña Unveils Three 'Historic' Industry Measures: USD 100 Million Credit Line, Fogain Guarantee Fund and MIC–Senatur Merger Bill (2026-09-18)
events.summary: At the 90th anniversary dinner of the Paraguayan Industrial Union (UIP), President Santiago Peña announced three measures to boost manufacturing. The 'Paraguay Industrial' credit line carries an initial fund of USD 100 million (G. 600,000 million) with rates of 10.5% in guaraníes and 8.5% in dollars, terms of up to 15 years, grace periods of up to three years and a ceiling of USD 2.5 million per company, channelled through financial intermediaries accredited by the Development Finance Agency (AFD) and earmarked for machinery, equipment, technology and infrastructure, with up to 20% usable as working capital. Peña also signed the decree creating Fogain, a guarantee fund for firms lacking sufficient collateral, and handed Congress president Basilio Núñez a bill merging the Ministry of Industry and Commerce (MIC) with the Tourism Secretariat (Senatur), granting legal recognition to Rediex and strengthening trade-defence powers. Industry Minister Marco Riquelme said 'the excuses are over'.

events.title: Isaías Fretes Sworn In as New Health Minister, Inheriting the Doctors' Settlement and the IPS Portfolio (2026-09-18)
events.summary: President Peña swore in Isaías Ricardo Fretes Zárate as Minister of Public Health and Social Welfare at the Government Palace, in a ceremony attended by Congress president Basilio Núñez and Chamber of Deputies president Raúl Latorre. Fretes was appointed by Decree No. 6889 of 13 September after chairing the IPS board. His appointment caps a turbulent period that saw 446 specialist resignations and a national doctors' strike, resolved days earlier with a package worth USD 260 million in additional 2027 medicines funding, a G. 2 million per-post salary rise and 2,300 permanent appointments. Fretes warned his successor at the IPS, Derlis León, about 'irregularities born of neglect' found on the institution's land in the Chaco, signalling the pension fund's governance is next on the reform agenda.

events.title: Peña Tells Honor Colorado to Freeze the 2028 Ticket Debate and Focus on the October 4 Municipal Vote (2026-09-18)
events.summary: President Peña publicly asked the Honor Colorado leadership to shelve the debate over the 2028 presidential ticket and concentrate resources on the 4 October municipal elections, backing the Lista 1 candidates. He said his relationship with Horacio Cartes 'is fine' and denied that Vice-President Pedro Alliana had left Honor Colorado. The intervention followed a week of visible internal friction: Cartes unilaterally named Juan Carlos Baruja as precandidate for vice-president for 2028, angering Alliana, while the Senate's information request on Ueno Bank — a bank historically linked to the Cartes group — was read by dissident deputy Roberto González as the trigger, with the remark that 'Horacio tweaked the President's ear'. Deputy Daniel Centurión blamed Cartes for the tension. The episode leaves the ruling coalition visibly strained 16 days before the municipal vote.

events.title: Municipal Campaign Enters the Final Stretch Under a Poll-Publication Blackout; Camilo Pérez Holds a Wide Lead in Asunción (2026-09-19)
events.summary: With the 4 October municipal elections two weeks away, candidates closed out the campaign week with territory-heavy operations, and the legal deadline for publishing opinion polls expired on 18 September. In Asunción, the ruling-party candidate Camilo Pérez (Lista 1) held his third zonal meeting in Barrio Jara with over a thousand supporters, claiming 94% name recognition and a roughly 20-point internal lead; surveys published before the blackout put him at 50.4–50.8% against Soledad Núñez's 27%. Pérez's rival challenged him to a debate, saying 'they are not giving him permission'. In Fernando de la Mora an Ati Snead poll (15–17 September, 500 respondents) put Ariel Ojeda at 42.7% versus 34.6% for Luis Fernando Franco. Liberal senator Éver Villalba raised concerns about the vulnerability of voting machines and demanded an audit of the TSJE equipment.

events.title: Government Defuses Teachers' Strike with a 5% Raise; Six Unions Accept, Four Press Ahead with a 48-Hour Walkout (2026-09-16)
events.summary: After negotiations between the education ministry (MEC), the finance ministry and teaching unions, the government offered a 5% salary increase for 2027 applied in two stages (2.4% already budgeted plus 2.6% from July 2027), with an estimated fiscal cost of USD 47 million. The FEP, which represents close to 80% of teachers, along with APE, ADP and Adofep accepted and lifted the measure. OTEP-SN, OTEP-A, UNE and MAS-MP rejected the offer, refused to sign, and ratified a 48-hour national strike for 17–18 September with a march from Plaza Batallón 40 to the finance ministry, demanding the 8% they call 'non-negotiable'. Education Minister Luis Ramírez said the ministry would seek a legal review of the limits of the action through a request to the labour ministry. The split marks the third front — after doctors and the budget — in the government's 2026 wage negotiations.

events.title: Dissident Unions Declare a Truce and Classes Resume Nationwide; Talks Shift to the Budget Bicameral (2026-09-18)
events.summary: The four unions that had gone ahead with the strike declared a 'cuarto intermedio' and lifted the measure, allowing public schools to return to normal activities on Friday 18 September. Education Minister Luis Ramírez confirmed all public institutions were back in class and that the dissident unions had ultimately joined the government's proposal. Union leaders framed the retreat as a tactical pause rather than a settlement: OTEP-SN's Blanca Ávalos said negotiations would continue on two tracks, with the MEC over workload and with the Budget Bicameral Commission over sector funding, while OTEP-A's Gabriel Espínola stressed no agreement had been signed and that demands on infrastructure investment, inclusive education and free public schooling remained live. The government's management of the dispute is now tied directly to the 2027 budget debate, where health and education compete for the same constrained fiscal space.

events.title: SINAMED Accepts the Government's Offer and Calls Off the September 21–22 National Doctors' Strike (2026-09-16)
events.summary: In an extraordinary assembly, the doctors' union SINAMED unanimously approved the government's proposal and formally lifted the 48-hour national strike scheduled for 21–22 September. The four-point deal covers USD 260 million in additional medicines and supplies in the 2027 budget; a G. 2 million salary increase per post paid progressively in 2027 (G. 500,000 in April, G. 500,000 in July and G. 1 million in December); the permanent appointment of 2,300 doctors with 1,500 further vacancies foreseen for 2027; and G. 1 million for working public holidays from January. SINAMED president Rossana González warned the union would mobilise again if the commitments are not honoured, and a special committee will lobby Congress. The agreement removes the most disruptive of the three social conflicts that have dominated the third quarter, but shifts the cost into the 2027 budget now under bicameral review.

events.title: Interior Ministry Reinforces Alto Paraná with 40 Lince Agents and 20 Motorcycles, Announces Drone and Camera Plan (2026-09-17)
events.summary: Interior Minister Enrique Riera led the handover of 20 motorcycles and 40 Lince tactical-group agents to reinforce the Alto Paraná police, adding to 40 locally based motorised officers for a total of 40 motorcycles and 80 agents. The deployment was presented in downtown Ciudad del Este with motorised patrols, and Riera announced the opening of a Lince headquarters in the department plus a departmental security plan built on drones and cameras. The reinforcement follows a period of high-profile crime in the tri-border area, including an armed assault on a currency exchanger in Asunción in which the perpetrators posed as economic-crimes investigators and took between USD 10,000 and 15,000, and a home robbery with hostage-taking in Itapúa that ended in a three-kilometre chase and shootout. Security on the eastern border remains a recurring concern for logistics and data-centre investors in the department.

events.title: Senate Foreign Relations Committee Unanimously Approves the Mercosur–EFTA Free Trade Agreement (2026-09-16)
events.summary: The Senate's Foreign Relations and International Affairs Committee unanimously approved the bill ratifying the free trade agreement between Mercosur and the EFTA states — Switzerland, Norway, Iceland and Liechtenstein — in a working session chaired by Senator Antonio Barrios with Industry and Commerce Minister Marco Riquelme in attendance. The agreement creates a free trade zone with tariff reduction and elimination commitments, national treatment, disciplines on quantitative restrictions and import licensing, agricultural preferences and specific quotas for sensitive products. Riquelme said the deal allows tariff-free trade and opens export and investment opportunities into high-purchasing-power markets demanding food, sustainable products, agro-industrial goods and differentiated manufactures. Senators singled out Norway as the priority market and stressed the need for an equitable distribution of quotas among Mercosur members — the same fault line blocking the EU agreement.

events.title: New Ambassador to Washington Puts the Beef Agenda First, Targeting up to 80,000 Tonnes for the US Market (2026-09-18)
events.summary: Ambassador Estefanía Laterza, ratified by the Senate as Paraguay's representative in Washington, made the beef agenda her first working priority in a meeting with the animal-health and quality service Senacsa. The United States opened an additional 300,000-tonne beef quota distributed in three monthly tranches of 100,000 tonnes between 1 September and 30 November; Paraguay aims to capture up to 10% of that volume. The country currently ships 6,000–8,000 tonnes per month, had accumulated 35,000 tonnes by 31 August and projects around 60,000 tonnes for the year, with the ambassador naming 80,000 tonnes and a shift toward higher-value cuts as the medium-term objective. The US is Paraguay's second-largest beef buyer with 35,443 tonnes worth USD 211.5 million so far this year plus 1,458 tonnes of by-products worth USD 6.96 million.

events.title: Paraguay Buys More Than USD 1 Million in US Munitions Under the FMS Programme; Ammunition Plant Reactivation Under Review (2026-09-16)
events.summary: Paraguay purchased more than USD 1 million in munitions from the United States through the Foreign Military Sales programme, and the government is evaluating the reactivation of a domestic ammunition factory. The purchase sits within a broader security and defence agenda that already includes the SOFA status-of-forces agreement, a third-country safe-haven arrangement, a migration memorandum, joint training and technology transfer against organised crime, and an understanding with a US university reserving 15 annual places for Paraguayan students administered through the anti-drugs secretariat Senad. A memorandum of understanding on nuclear energy, linked to diversifying the energy matrix, research and academic exchange, was also recently signed. The deepening defence relationship complements the trade track led by Ambassador Laterza, who has set out six workstreams including political relations, the economic and commercial agenda, security and defence, and science and innovation.

events.title: Spanish Technology Mission and Argentine Trade Mission Converge on Asunción in the Same Week (2026-09-17)
events.summary: Two foreign business missions arrived in Asunción on the same day. A Spanish technology delegation of 27 representatives from 17 companies active in artificial intelligence, software, automation and digital transformation explored partnership and establishment opportunities; Rediex vice-minister Eduardo Gustale noted exports are growing at around 26% and that Paraguay is no longer dependent on agriculture alone. Separately, an Argentine mission of 16 firms and 28 businesspeople in construction, hardware and refrigeration sought associations, distribution agreements or relocation to Paraguay. The convergence illustrates the country's dual pull: as a low-tax, low-energy-cost production base for regional firms and as an emerging digital-services destination. It also raises the competitive stakes for local partners and for suppliers positioning around the data-centre and industrial build-out.

events.title: Paraguay Day in New York Draws the Largest Business Delegation in the Country's History, but the MIC Admits an Energy Bottleneck (2026-09-17)
events.summary: Industry and Commerce Minister Marco Riquelme led more than 50 Paraguayan business representatives — the largest such delegation in the country's history — to New York for investment days organised with Bank of America and J.P. Morgan, targeting forest industry, logistics, energy and manufacturing. Riquelme openly acknowledged an energy bottleneck: projects representing more than 7,000 megawatts are waiting for connection, equivalent to Paraguay's entire share of Itaipú output. He said this requires modernising ANDE and opening power generation to private capital. The admission is significant because energy availability is the central premise of the country's pitch to data-centre and AI investors, and it aligns with warnings from the state utility that the Itaipú surplus could be exhausted toward 2030 without new generation.

sections.title: V. Industry Focus: Telecom, Digital Energy & AI

events.title: MITIC Proposes a Regulatory Sandbox for AI and Insists Data-Protection and Cybersecurity Laws Must Come First (2026-09-16)
events.summary: In a public hearing, ICT Minister Gustavo Villate proposed creating a regulatory sandbox for artificial intelligence — a controlled testing environment — rather than a standalone AI statute. Participants agreed that a personal data protection law and a cybersecurity law must be enacted first as the foundation of trust. Villate outlined the institutional split between cyber-defence under the Ministry of Defence and the civil-public-private sphere managed by MITIC's General Directorate of Cybersecurity, with the CERT now operating on continuous 24/7 monitoring. He presented the same framework at the 49th CITEL CCP.I meeting held in Asunción on 7–11 September, where he called cybersecurity one of the greatest global challenges and cited work with the OAS to update the 2024–2025 National Cybersecurity Plan, and at the Diplomatic and Consular Academy, where he positioned the data-protection and cybersecurity agenda as a prerequisite for Paraguay's ambition to become a technology hub.

events.title: HIVE Reports 300 MW Contracted in Paraguay and Targets 400 MW by Year-End, as Crypto and AI Loads Seek Tariff Certainty to 2037 (2026-09-17)
events.summary: HIVE Digital reports 300 MW contracted across its 100 MW Valenzuela and 200 MW Yguazú plants in Paraguay, with a target of 400 MW by the end of 2026, and is converting its Tier 1 facilities to Tier 3 to offer HPC and AI cloud services. The company and other members of the Special Intensive Consumption Group are asking ANDE to extend their preferential supply contracts from the current expiry of 31 December 2027 out to 2037; HIVE's Paraguay president Gabriel Lamas said the industry operates on an interruptible basis and does not compete for residential or industrial supply, and that ten-year visibility is needed to raise capital for a path to 1,000 MW. ANDE has held firm on 2027 as a non-extendable deadline. Energy expert Ricardo Canese counters that the tariff should be around USD 80/MWh rather than the current USD 44/MWh, estimating the annual benefit at USD 284 million, and notes crypto-mining generates 0.83 jobs per MW against a national average of 721.

events.title: Independent Study Recommends a 39.4% Accumulated Rise in ANDE Tariffs by 2030 as Itaipú Negotiation Looms (2026-09-15)
events.summary: A technical study by CEARE-UBA with backing from the Inter-American Development Bank recommends an accumulated 39.4% increase in ANDE's tariffs applied in stages between 2026 and 2030, lifting the average tariff from about USD 49.2/MWh to USD 68.6/MWh, to close a financial gap of roughly USD 2 billion; other references cite increases of up to 45.6%. The Executive and ANDE stressed it is a technical analysis only and that residential users will not face increases this year, with any change requiring a political decision. The debate is inseparable from Itaipú: the tariff has been frozen at USD 19.28 per kW/month for 2024–2026, President Peña wants a three-year fixed tariff and has said Paraguay will not accept a reduction after 2026, against the 2024 bilateral agreement with Brazil that the tariff should reflect only Annex C operating costs from 2027. A new tariff at that level would cost ANDE around USD 73 million a year.

events.title: Paraguay Tech Week 2026 Draws Venture Funds from More Than 20 Countries, Showcasing the Country as an AI and Data-Centre Sandbox (2026-09-13)
events.summary: The third edition of the VC & Startups Summit, held as part of Paraguay Tech Week 2026, brought together entrepreneurs and investment funds from more than 20 countries. Participants highlighted low tax burden, cheap renewable energy and the country's recent investment-grade ratings as the combination attracting technology companies, and described Paraguay as an ideal sandbox for developing data centres and artificial intelligence with regional reach. The event reinforces the government's positioning strategy around the Yguazú Digital sovereign AI computing project with Taiwan and the Distrito Innova technology park next to the Taiwan–Paraguay Polytechnic University, both of which remain at feasibility or construction stage. The optimism is tempered by the same constraint flagged elsewhere in the week: waiting lists for grid connection exceeding 7,000 MW and an unresolved tariff framework for intensive consumers.

events.title: Claro Reports 5G Coverage Across Eight Cities and 100 Radiobases Built with Nokia Equipment (2026-09-18)
events.summary: Claro Paraguay, the first operator to launch commercial 5G in the country in December 2025, reports coverage now spanning the central zone plus Coronel Oviedo, Villarrica, Pedro Juan Caballero, Hernandarias, Ciudad del Este, Encarnación and Cambyretá. Technology director Raúl Aguilera said the company had installed 50 base stations by the end of 2025 and was completing the remaining 50 through mid-2026 to meet the 100-radiobase obligation attached to its 200 MHz in the 3.5 GHz band, with 10% reserved for state institutions. The deployment uses Nokia's AirScale 5G portfolio with ReefShark chipsets, Massive MIMO radios and IPAA+ antennas. Directorgeneral Alfredo Alcaraz cited the availability of compatible handsets as the main obstacle to mass adoption, and the company lists five-year licence terms as its principal regulatory complaint, against a total planned investment of USD 35 million over the first licence period.

events.title: Tigo Nears Its February 2027 5G Launch Deadline with 2.3 GHz Spectrum and a USD 100 Million Infrastructure Financing (2026-09-16)
events.summary: Tigo, Millicom's Paraguayan brand, won the 2.3–2.4 GHz band in the second 5G auction for USD 1.6 million, adding to the 50 MHz it already holds in 2300/2600 MHz. The licence carries a 90-day deadline to file the detailed engineering project and 180 days to switch on commercial service, putting a hard launch date in February 2027, with deployments expected to begin before the end of 2026. Tigo must build 100 base stations within four years plus 10 for state institutions within two. The operator is funded by a USD 100 million private bond placement by IDB Invest and Proparco announced in March 2026 to accelerate 4G/4.5G/5G and fibre rollouts. In August the antitrust authority CONACOM cleared Atis Group's acquisition of 281 Millicom towers under a sale-and-leaseback that keeps Tigo as the anchor tenant, monetising passive infrastructure ahead of the 5G build.

events.title: Personal Wins 3.7 GHz 5G Spectrum and Extends Its Fixed-Internet Lead for a Fifth Consecutive Year (2026-09-16)
events.summary: Personal, the Núcleo S.A. subsidiary of Argentina's Telecom, took the 3.7–3.8 GHz band in the second 5G auction for USD 1 million and faces the same February 2027 commercial launch deadline and 100-radiobase obligation as Tigo. In parallel, the 2026 nPerf fixed-internet barometer ranked Personal first for the fifth consecutive year with average download speeds of 148.39 Mbps and a score of 103,262, ahead of Claro at 114.21 Mbps and Tigo at 84.30 Mbps. Personal offers fibre plans up to 400 Mbps down and 100 Mbps up and is described as running one of the most aggressive fibre expansions in the market, with pricing between USD 35 and USD 70. The operator's combination of fixed-network leadership and mid-band 5G spectrum positions it strongly in the enterprise and wholesale segments that feed data-centre and cloud demand.
events.client_tag: Personal / Núcleo S.A. — 5G licence & fixed-network leadership

events.title: Comptroller Finds No Evidence Nubicom Is Deploying Its Required Radiobases, With Only One Site Confirmed (2026-09-14)
events.summary: The Comptroller General (CGR) has advised that there is insufficient evidence that Nubicom is deploying the 22 radiobases required in the first year of its 3.5 GHz licence, with only one operational base station confirmed in the Villa Morra neighbourhood of Asunción. The CGR gave CONATEL five working days to respond and criticised the absence of a detailed monitoring mechanism, while clarifying that at this stage it cannot conclude that the deployment commitment has been breached — only that there is a 'weakness of control and traceability'. Earlier findings in the special audit include documents filed after the deadline, validation of the 100,000 active-subscriber requirement through a sworn statement without independent confirmation, and the absence of verified sector experience or minimum financial capacity. Nubicom, linked to itti Saeca and the Grupo Vázquez, committed to roughly USD 78 million in investment and promotes an Open RAN 5G standalone deployment. Licence cancellation remains on the table.

events.title: Copaco-Vox: State Operator Seeks Private Capital as Vox Posts Negative Equity of G. 85,609 Million (2026-09-16)
events.summary: The new president of state operators Copaco and Vox, Rodrigo Ferreira, inherits a deepening financial crisis. Vox recorded a net loss of G. 33,314 million, negative net equity of G. 85,609 million and debts of more than G. 178,316 million to Copaco; Copaco itself has lost over 200,000 fixed-line customers in six years. The government says it will prioritise attracting private capital in a 'shared risk' structure rather than outright privatisation, and has not produced a rescue plan after the deadline expired. Union representatives warn of a 'sweep' at Copaco-Vox, while a national roaming bill before the Chamber of Deputies is viewed favourably only by Copaco, since it would let Vox use rival coverage without further investment. The operator's roughly 12,000 km of fibre plus 2,500 km at Vox and 400 sites remain the state's principal wholesale infrastructure assets.

sections.title: VII. Integrated Impact Analysis for Business Operations
sections.impact_analysis:
🟡 The Currency Is Still the Single Dominant Operating Variable. The September EVE survey published on 17 September has analysts cutting their end-2026 inflation forecast to 3.0% and projecting the guaraní at G. 6,100/USD by December — a slight weakening from spot levels near G. 5,915–5,920, but still far below the G. 6,600 at which the year opened. Every revenue line denominated in dollars converts at roughly 20% less than a year ago. The soy complex illustrates the mechanic precisely: volumes set records, with 7,413,675 tonnes of grain shipped through August worth USD 2,886 million, about USD 907 million more than in 2025, yet exporter margins compress because the same dollars buy fewer guaraníes. Beef is the counter-example, with export values down 7% on volumes down nearly 24% even as the average price rose to USD 6,972 per tonne. Budget any 2026–2027 local-currency projection off a G. 6,100–6,300 range, not the G. 5,900 spot, and stress-test both ends.

🟡 The Fiscal Squeeze Is Now the Binding Constraint on Every Government Decision. The three social conflicts of the third quarter all resolved in the same week of 13–20 September — teachers accepting a 5% raise costing USD 47 million, doctors accepting a package worth USD 260 million in 2027 medicines funding plus G. 2 million per post and 2,300 permanent appointments — and all three now land on the 2027 budget being reviewed by the Budget Bicameral Commission, whose report is due by the end of October. Against a fiscal deficit the IMF puts at 3.5% of GDP for 2026 and a 2027 proposal that asks Congress for a temporary exception to the Fiscal Responsibility Law to reach 3.9%, the government has simultaneously promised industry a USD 100 million credit line, a guarantee fund and a MIC–Senatur merger, and has committed to bond issuance of USD 2,708 million in 2027, 70% more than this year. Public-sector payment discipline and the timing of any capital spending should be treated as at risk, particularly for suppliers with exposure to health, education and infrastructure budgets.

🟡 Energy, Not Demand, Is the Binding Constraint on New Investment. The most consequential statement of the week was Industry Minister Marco Riquelme's admission at Paraguay Day in New York that more than 7,000 MW of projects are waiting for grid connection — equivalent to Paraguay's entire share of Itaipú output — and that this requires modernising ANDE and opening generation to private capital. This sits alongside an independent IDB-backed study recommending a 39.4% accumulated tariff increase by 2030, an unresolved Itaipú tariff negotiation with Brazil, ANDE's refusal to extend preferential contracts beyond 31 December 2027, and HIVE's push for ten-year visibility to fund a path from 300 MW to 1,000 MW. For any supplier or contractor whose pipeline depends on data-centre, crypto-mining or electro-intensive load growth, the risk has shifted from demand to interconnection timing, tariff design and contract tenor.

🟢 Telecom Capex Is Committed and Time-Bound. Both Tigo and Personal have a hard February 2027 commercial launch deadline and a 100-radiobase obligation each, on top of Claro's USD 35 million first-phase programme and its 100 base stations, largely Nokia-built. Tigo has secured USD 100 million through an IDB Invest/Proparco bond and monetised 281 towers through the Atis sale-and-leaseback. This is the most predictable demand pool in the market, but it is also the shortest — the build window closes before 2027, after which spending shifts from coverage to capacity. Nubicom remains the outlier and the credit risk, with the Comptroller unable to evidence more than one operational site out of the 22 required.

🟢 Trade Access Is Widening on Multiple Fronts Simultaneously. The Senate's Foreign Relations Committee unanimously approved the Mercosur–EFTA agreement on 16 September; the US opened a 300,000-tonne beef quota with Paraguay targeting 10%; the new ambassador to Washington is prioritising a path to 80,000 tonnes; and Spanish and Argentine business missions arrived in the same week. None of these translate into near-term revenue, but they materially improve the medium-term addressable market for logistics, cold chain, processing equipment and agri-industrial supply.

sections.title: VIII. Targeted Recommendations for Chinese Enterprises
sections.impact_analysis:
🔴 The Taiwan Alignment Is Now Structurally Embedded in Procurement. The clearest signal of the week is the second 5G auction outcome: Tigo took 2.3 GHz with Nokia equipment and Personal took 3.7 GHz, while Claro's 3.5 GHz network is also Nokia-built. The tender rules required bidders to come from countries maintaining diplomatic relations with Paraguay, which excluded Chinese vendors, and Chinese firms did not obtain licences in either round. President Peña has publicly attributed criticism of the auctions to Chinese government pressure. The same logic is being institutionalised in the Yguazú Digital sovereign AI compute project with Taiwan, whose memoranda contemplate diplomatic-grade privileges for data infrastructure. Assume exclusion from state-linked and licensed-operator 5G core and RAN procurement, and plan through indirect channels — enterprise networking, towers and passive infrastructure, power and cooling for data centres, fibre, and distribution relationships with the operators that did win.

🟡 China Remains the Largest Trading Partner Without Formal Relations, and the Asymmetry Is Growing More Visible. China supplies 36.4% of Paraguay's imports, more than any other origin, while bilateral trade runs through triangulation. The external affairs ministry has stated China records 'zero imports' of Paraguayan soy, and estimates put the cost of triangulation at around USD 45 per tonne with annual losses of USD 400–600 million across the soy chain. Paraguay's own position, restated by Foreign Minister Rubén Ramírez Lezcano, is that it will trade with China only if Taiwan ties are untouched — a 'red line' Beijing rejects. Expect continued pressure from Paraguayan agricultural exporters and importers for formal links, and treat the issue as a live but slow-moving one that will not resolve inside this budget cycle.

🟡 The Fiscal Constraint Means Public-Sector Payment Risk Is Real. With the 2027 budget requesting an exception to the Fiscal Responsibility Law to run a 3.9% deficit, USD 2,708 million of planned bond issuance and the government simultaneously honouring teacher, doctor and industrial commitments, the stock of floating debt and the pace of supplier payments warrant active monitoring. The week's most concrete warning was the new health minister flagging 'irregularities born of neglect' in IPS assets. Before extending credit terms to public buyers, verify the specific budget line and current payment history rather than relying on sovereign-level assurances.

🟢 Positioning Opportunities That Do Not Require Political Alignment. Energy Minister-level admissions that 7,000 MW of load cannot be connected and that ANDE needs private generation create a genuine opening in grid equipment, substations, transformers, transmission and distribution hardware, metering and demand management — all areas where Chinese suppliers compete on cost and delivery time without touching the 5G procurement exclusion. Likewise, the 39.4–45.6% tariff adjustment debate implies substantial ANDE capital investment ahead. Data-centre cooling, power distribution and enclosures for HIVE's Tier 3 conversion and similar builds are addressable through commercial channels. Finally, the Spanish and Argentine missions targeting construction, hardware and refrigeration indicate competitive pressure is intensifying in exactly the distributor and SMB segments that have historically been a natural entry point — move early on partner selection or expect to be pre-empted.

🟢 Governance and Social Risk Are Lower Than the Headlines Suggest. All three major social conflicts — teachers, doctors and the budget fight — de-escalated within the window, with the doctors' 21–22 September strike explicitly called off and classes resuming on 18 September. The remaining near-term political risk is the 4 October municipal election and the visible strain inside Honor Colorado between the Cartes and Peña camps, which will not affect commercial operations but can slow appointments and approvals in the weeks either side of the vote. The Alto Paraná security reinforcement — 40 Lince agents, 20 motorcycles and a drone and camera plan — is a positive signal for personnel safety around Ciudad del Este logistics and industrial sites.
